source.title: Unveiling the structure of wide flat minima in neural networks
source.authors: Carlo Baldassi; Clarissa Lauditi; E. M. Malatesta; Gabriele Perugini; R. Zecchina

record.file_problem: Full paper and supplemental material are present. The supplied text includes flattened figure captions and plotted results.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures local entropy, margin, and local energy profiles in tractable binary networks, and reports deep-network experiments relevant to flatness and generalization. It does not directly measure the training–test generalization gap from the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper's central analytical results concern solution geometry in random-pattern classification. Its numerical deep-network experiments report train error, overlaps, and local energy after weight perturbations, not test error. Rows capture measured margin/distance or local-energy outcomes only where they bear on the versions' named properties. Cited studies' results are not recorded.
record.test_reason: The study derives solution-space geometry in binary networks and measures training errors, solution overlaps, and training-error responses to random weight flips. It reports no held-out performance or generalization gaps. These results therefore do not test V7's sharpness–gap correlation or any other listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that dense solution regions in their nonconvex binary-network models arise where high-margin solutions concentrate and connect through lower-margin solutions. They also propose a geometric estimate of the algorithmic capacity threshold and describe the deep binary-network experiments as consistent with this scenario; those experiments do not establish a relationship with held-out generalization.
record.recipe_differences: Analytical replica calculations and numerical perturbation experiments in binary-weight networks; no direct generalization-gap measurement or intervention matching the listed versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The local-entropy transition varies with load α and with architecture and activation: the reported threshold differs between ReLU and sign committee machines. Deep-network experiments vary dataset, architecture, and training-set size.

fits_no_version.finding: In the random-pattern binary perceptron, typical solutions become closer in Hamming distance as imposed margin increases, although their number decreases exponentially.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Higher-margin solutions in the studied binary perceptron are rarer but less dispersed.

fits_no_version.finding: Positive-margin reference solutions have dense neighborhoods of lower-margin solutions. Their local-entropy profiles change with margin and pattern load; sufficiently high loads disrupt the extended dense-region geometry.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Margin and pattern load govern the geometry and fragmentation of dense solution regions in the studied binary networks.

fits_no_version.finding: The calculated transition to non-monotonic local-entropy profiles occurs near load 0.773 for ReLU committee machines and 0.558 for sign committee machines.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The dense-region transition depends on the activation function in binary committee machines.

fits_no_version.finding: Binary MLPs trained on MNIST odd/even, FashionMNIST, and CIFAR-10 reach distinct, widely separated solutions even near their training-set capacity. Zero-training-error solutions near that threshold have local training-error profiles the authors interpret as flat.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Binary MLPs can have multiple separated solutions with flat local training-error profiles near their algorithmic fitting threshold.

record.problems: The main generalization-related evidence is indirect: analytical results use an idealized random-pattern binary perceptron, and the deep-network experiments do not report test error. The replica-symmetric computation may be approximate; the authors report numerical instability and inability to test nontrivial 1RSB solutions at small distances. Deep-network results are shown in figures and captions, with no test-set comparison.
record.rows_left_out: No result rows were retained: the study reports no outcome directly measuring the training–test gap or a listed version's test-error behavior. Deep-network figure outcomes are described qualitatively in text and are represented under fits_no_version.

untested.parts: Coexistence of random-label fitting and natural-label generalization under the same architecture and training recipe, including chance-level held-out accuracy for random labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected held-out performance and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer held-out performance under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout's effects on held-out error across training-set sizes, dropout strengths, and augmentation conditions.

Correlation of magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance with training–test gaps, and its ranking performance against norm- and margin-based measures. Training-error perturbation profiles alone do not establish this relationship.
Test-accuracy effects of removing highly memorized examples compared with removing equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Correct the record's tests/T2 classification and V7 tested_not_extracted status: no listed version is tested. The study discusses prior flatness–generalization findings, but its own results concern solution geometry and training behavior. The empty row set is appropriate, and no omitted result bearing directly on a listed version was found.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fit versus natural-label generalization and chance-level held-out accuracy.
Width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold and resulting test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected test error and effects of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer test performance.
The paper studies margin and local entropy, but does not measure magnitude-aware weight perturbation tolerance or compare such a measure with generalization gaps.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.
